name: One-pot cottage & garlic-confit pasta (פסטה קוטג' ושום קונפי)

source.author: Pasted recipe (Hebrew)
source.notes: Same one-pot method as the ptitim rosé risotto: 500 g dry pasta cooked straight in a wide pot with 1 kg cottage 5%, 150 g grated 9% yellow cheese, 3 tbsp garlic confit + 1 tbsp of its oil, salt, pepper, chili flakes and 2–3 cups water; served with a drizzle of confit oil, parmesan and fresh herbs. Analyzed as 8 servings with regular (white) pasta; garnish counted as ~1 tbsp confit oil and ~20 g parmesan across the pot. Garlic confit counted as soft cloves with some absorbed oil. Manual intake — reference only, not adopted. Estimate.

ingredients.note: white pasta assumed — whole-wheat/spelt adds fibre
the cheeses are already salty — see mods

steps: Put the pasta in a wide pot; spread the cottage, yellow cheese and garlic confit over it, add the confit oil and season with salt, pepper and chili.
Pour 2 cups water evenly over the pot and stir lightly so it reaches the bottom.
Cover and bring to a boil on high; once boiling, stir gently so the pasta doesn't stick.
Lower to medium-low and cook covered 4–5 min; uncover, stir and adjust with ¼–½ cup water if dry (or remove some liquid if too wet).
Cook uncovered 8–10 min more until the pasta is done and the sauce is thick and coating; turn off, cover and rest 5 min.
Serve hot with a little confit oil, grated parmesan and fresh herbs.

batch_totals.note: Whole pot (8 servings). Nearly identical profile to the original ptitim rosé risotto: the kilo of cottage carries the protein, the pasta carries most of the calories, and sodium is high because 1½ tsp salt goes on top of cottage, yellow cheese and parmesan.

him.verdict: A creamy, comforting one-pot pasta with ~28 g protein per serving thanks to the kilo of cottage — but still pasta-led (~53 g carbs, ~6.2 g protein per 100 kcal), low in fibre, and high in sodium (~1,000 mg/serving), mostly from salt added on top of already-salty cheeses. No vegetables at all as written.
flags: high sodium (~1,000 mg) — 1½ tsp salt + cheeses
suggested_mods: Same fixes as the optimized ptitim risotto: whole-wheat/spelt pasta cut to 400 g, cottage 3%, 100 g yellow cheese, no added salt, and fold in spinach + mushrooms/zucchini
Skip the extra confit-oil drizzle at serving (−~15 kcal/serving) — the confit cloves already carry the garlic flavour
Finish with lemon zest + herbs instead of salt

her_preconception.verdict: Good protein and calcium, pasteurized cheeses, fully cooked — no safety flags. But high sodium and essentially no folate or iron as written; folding in spinach would make it a solid option for her. Homemade garlic confit should be kept refrigerated and used within about a week (botulism risk if stored at room temperature).

safety_advisories.note: Homemade garlic confit (garlic in oil) must be refrigerated and used within ~1 week — stored at room temperature it carries a botulism risk.
safety_advisories.swap: make small batches and keep them cold, or use fresh garlic

suggested_mods: Fold in spinach for folate + iron

cooking_guide: Use a WIDE pot so the pasta cooks in an even layer and the cottage doesn't scorch underneath.
Stir right down to the bottom as soon as it boils — this is the moment pasta and cottage stick.
Short shapes (penne, fusilli, rigatoni) work best for one-pot; long pasta clumps.
Add water only ¼ cup at a time; it's easy to overshoot into soup.
Hold the salt until the end and taste — the cheeses usually season it enough.
Take it off slightly looser than you want; it thickens during the 5-minute rest. Reheat with a splash of water.
